body:
#

Hi Peter —
[**I’m writing to ask, humbly, if you will chip in $5 to my reelection campaign ahead of our important FEC fundraising deadline this Wednesday.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-dec25.lXrKfY&refcode=em251229-1-f&t=1&akid=1347%2E5691347%2Ez2EeSt)
Here’s why this request is so important, especially today:
The end of this month marks the most important fundraising deadline we’ve faced so far in our campaign, and one of the most critical tests of the movement we’ve built in Georgia.
After the deadline, we’re legally required to report our fundraising numbers to the Federal Election Commission — and shortly after, those numbers will be made public.
Everyone from Donald Trump to my Republican opponents and their billionaire allies are going to look at our fundraising numbers closely. Very closely.
If they think we look weak, you can bet they’ll flood the airwaves with even more attack ads designed to distort my record. Attacks we can’t afford this early in the campaign.
We have to show everyone that our movement in Georgia is thriving and unstoppable — that we have what it takes to build the strongest voter outreach and mobilization program our state has ever seen. Because that’s what it’s going to take to win this race.
That’s why I’m personally asking:
[**Will you make a contribution to my campaign before our critical FEC deadline Wednesday night? Every donation counts. Each one sends a powerful message that people like you have my back.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-dec25.lXrKfY&refcode=em251229-1-f&t=2&akid=1347%2E5691347%2Ez2EeSt)

Thank you for everything.
Jon

body:
Peter,

We're officially just days away from the election year, and time is running out for us to end the year strong.

Here's the truth: Everything we do at In This Together PAC happens because people like you choose to support our mission to invest in common sense, people-first candidates running in tough districts.

Your support is the reason we can recruit, train, and lift up candidates who actually listen to their communities — _not the ones chasing headlines, political division, or special-interest money._

As we head into 2026, the stakes couldn't be higher. We're fighting to elect leaders who will put people ahead of politics, lead with honesty and respect, and push back against the extremism, hate and division that have come to define so much of modern politics. Illinois State Rep. Joe Sosnowski, R-Rockford.
By Illinois Review

Illinois politics has a way of rewarding selective memory, and this past week delivered a near-perfect example.

Republican State Rep. Joe Sosnowski, Rockford – who voted for one of the largest tax increases in state history – has been honored by Americans for Prosperity Illinois as a champion of taxpayers.

In 2019, Sosnowski was one of just 20 House Republicans who voted in favor of Senate Bill 1939, the gas tax increase that formed the backbone of Gov. JB Pritzker’s “Rebuild Illinois” capital plan.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/12/gop-state-rep-joe-sosnowski-who-backed-illinois-gas-tax-hike-praised-as-taxpayer-defender-by-afp-illinois.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=afb5c18262-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
That vote helped Democrats double the state’s gas tax overnight and lock Illinois drivers into automatic increases tied to inflation.

Despite that record, Americans for Prosperity Illinois recently handed Sosnowski its 2025 Prairie State Promise Award. AFP went even further, claiming Sosnowski “exemplifies courageous, solutions-driven leadership and remains a dependable voice for Illinois taxpayers.”

body:

Cori Bush here.
As we head into our ONLY end-of-year deadline before the election, I’m very clear-eyed about what we’re up against, and even clearer about what we’re building.
Last cycle, AIPAC and their allies poured $15 million into St. Louis to lie about me and try to silence our movement, and now we know 63% of my opponent’s money this year came from AIPAC bundlers...
But here’s the part they didn’t count on. The New York Times recently reported what we’ve felt all along: AIPAC’s grip is slipping. No matter how much money they throw around, they can’t stop a movement rooted in truth and powered by the people.
They thought that if they spent enough money, they could push me out, slow me down, and make an example of what happens when you stand up to power.
They were wrong.
They thought giving me time away from Congress would weaken my voice? Instead, it sharpened it.
I’m not just running for myself, I’m running for all of us. For progressives. For families. For everyone who refuses to let billionaires and special interests crush real change.
In fact, the last time I was in Congress, I flipped a few tables and ruffled more than a few feathers, all in the name of good trouble and on behalf of the people of St. Louis.
And I’m back, just as I promised. Stronger. Louder. More determined than ever.
Our primary election is August 4, 2026 . It may sound far away, but when billionaires are already pouring money into my opponent’s campaign, we know the truth:
It’s big money versus a movement they could never buy, and winning will take all of us. Knocking doors. Making calls. Showing up for our neighbors.
This is our only end-of-year deadline of the cycle [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251229_newcongresswoman_eoy2_act] , and how we close it out will send a message about the kind of Congress we’re fighting for in the year ahead.
Can you make sure we meet our goals, finish strong, and show AIPAC we have what it takes to win by donating $25, or whatever you can afford, before our only end-of-year deadline? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251229_newcongresswoman_eoy2_act]

But now, with the [official End-Of-Year Deadline](https://links.trueamericanconservatives.com/s/c/-JYgt6fB3QSIMD154xwcECFMUCBO8V_a_0xhqIC3fo8-Jw0co2E9iLXAAuMtsr84BH61eSlEQ_jMtkaiaXNntzcwTTzePJtiE6DIkpw_s8jGAmapRtX46fm-77my2rVNLJxTir5a5hCf75PiMkMhmxR6-nhvKotYwLxw_giaN5I9kQuk8tVuA3-ui0FTHpllmZTabr78FuaSmNINwZBHdC3Geq4juIj_nWLL0yh7xF2yoVKgV1hYtJYLOhX4JEbSB8KvGF_0qSaVY0BlpX86CESzd8qIqXUIMTXbp-jyQfRlOQmKzK9JY1Fhr3i4rz018HRLy1XUynRBlE8He4FFap6jdV2kZis6ptcyjz4V4AyrOmFeRl7Cxe0uWBraUOio9zesfYsfMLEXcw_paPzzskfqtWtOwMmZ5bj2RNYQsvJg9N29dJsVxp859lHzp3wscC8N8Vzo-yEXT9XrAArcTNoYlFM69XoQdfob1FRx_jIKHQjSO4orpnG_PILg_zXfJKazo8Q01UuPv6yQsNaBhhY0vqhUDM-hPBCBbR0vNj9hbdTB9UA2XWwHy7bHgmVXtmusN4vKL13IQq2MTL9U/BE6vJGVlT3b2507TkaCICD_NQ7XYGZJ6/16) approaching, we must close 2025 how we started it: with strength and momentum. Thanks to patriots like you, we have closed the gap significantly on our 2025 fundraising goal. **We are now just $9,700 away from hitting our critical End-Of-Year target.** Hitting our goal would be a huge moral victory, yes. But it's more. We must enter 2026 with the resources for:
* Massive voter outreach from Eureka to San Diego.

name: Justin Streiff, Turning Point USA
subject: The book Charlie left behind
body:
Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

| | | [](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zv8l6grd969leaiqehnvden40388gulslk2ikc3g_rp22sh2s8i6eor7c1gmco74cdh2bs)
---
| | Friend,
---
| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...
---
[](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zd10lflviaiff9rnasrr53pkuiu0elma2rqm1df8_rp22sh2s8i6eor7c1gmco74cdh2bs)
---
This was Charlie's final message. His final act of trust.

A book not about politics... but about peace.

**It 's called: _Stop, in the Name of God._**

**[And right now, when you make a gift of ANY amount to Turning Point USA, we'll send you a copy -- as our thank-you for carrying Charlie's mission forward.](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zqr02gd2dbur1pslit38vs7oke4k2tiesmc7e3u8_rp22sh2s8i6eor7c1gmco74cdh2bs)**
---
[ **Support Turning Point USA**
**& Receive Charlie's Final Book**](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zea66q5ltspd8sbpqaku620v78qk5jpjjd68tkqg_rp22sh2s8i6eor7c1gmco74cdh2bs)
---
Friend, like I mentioned, this isn't a political book.

It's not a culture war manifesto.

It's a call to stop.

To rest. To breathe. To return to God.

**Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. **

Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away.

Trust that God is in control.

Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship.

**In _Stop, in the Name of God,_ you'll discover: **

🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout

🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer

🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation

Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again.

That's the heartbeat of his final message.

**[To claim your copy of this life-changing book, simply make a generous gift in any amount to Turning Point USA today.](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zcrq4hh6t803tcng8th43hqcc5m3bd9pufr0c1bo_rp22sh2s8i6eor7c1gmco74cdh2bs)**
---
[ **Support Turning Point USA**
**& Receive Charlie's Final Book**](http://e.icyminews.com/rd/9z2zo1vsgajb0nq5utj9vlr7qjej920olgvcgtleg4g_rp22sh2s8i6eor7c1gmco74cdh2bs)
---
Charlie Kirk didn't waste his time on earth.

He left behind a family. He left behind a movement. And he left behind this truth...

For anyone ready to step off the treadmill... and walk back toward what's eternal.

Friend, thank you -- in advance -- for helping reach the next generation with truth, faith, and moral courage.

These are the very things Charlie gave his life for.

May the message he left behind lead you -- just as it led him -- to a deeper trust in God...

A stronger love for your family...

And a renewed peace in your own soul.
---
**For Charlie, **

**Justin Streiff **
Chief Operating Officer
Turning Point USA

name: Mike Bouchard
subject: Would you jump?

When the plane door opens at 1,200 feet, most people freeze.
Paratroopers don’t.
You step forward into the wind, the uncertainty, the danger — because the mission depends on it. You don’t wait. You don’t hesitate. **You jump.**
That mindset shaped everything in my life:
ROTC at Michigan State.
20 days’ notice to deploy to Iraq.
Leading missions to defeat ISIS.
Protecting thousands of Americans overseas.
And now — stepping into this race for Congress.
This campaign is another kind of jump. And the truth is: **I’m standing at the door again.**
**Because tonight is my first-ever end-of-year fundraising deadline, and once that clock hits zero, the report becomes permanent. Unchangeable. Final. GREEN LIGHT IS LIT.**

| Peter, I’m about to ask you to [_**mark the end of 2025 with a donation before the end-of-year fundraising deadline.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/122191376/591850906/1120488449?amount=25&refcode=RS_EM_FR_2025.12.29_EOY1_90do&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NzI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMjQzOTU5Zi1kNWU0LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Tx5MXLzZtJT2h1iN8EUdqhIRk5l_j4MfVJQOGT4drRY=) But first, let’s talk about this year – my first in Congress. We talked about healthcare costs, Medicaid, and how folks can afford next month’s rent or save for retirement. And I heard that **Democrats have a responsibility to be bold, throw out the old playbook, and step into the future.** So that’s what my team and I did. The next census in less than 6 years away. They think you and I will be so relieved to see the border secure again and criminal illegal aliens deported, that you and I will be oblivious to this threat lying dormant under our very eyes. No way. My name is Rebecca Weber. But there's good news, too: Seven states have _expressly_ banned non-citizen voting already: Alabama, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Louisiana, North Dakota, and Ohio. **What 's more, voters approve of constitutional amendments to ban non-citizen voting by overwhelming margins. subject: The book Charlie left behind
body:
Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

| | | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2znr42ut1oe0isamngtn5f7o5p7jmop69lk6f7ma8_rp22sh2s8i6eor7c1gm2pr2c3h2bs)
---
| | Friend,
---
| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2ztsaenp0f424s8f3svmp8rsg240ummdhlsbh4bv0_rp22sh2s8i6eor7c1gm2pr2c3h2bs)
---
This was Charlie's final message. His final act of trust.

A book not about politics... but about peace.

**It 's called: _Stop, in the Name of God._**

**[And right now, when you make a gift of ANY amount to Turning Point USA, we'll send you a copy -- as our thank-you for carrying Charlie's mission forward.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zcujbn70b25bghguuooqici2lual6ufr57a4ujp8_rp22sh2s8i6eor7c1gm2pr2c3h2bs)**

---
Friend, like I mentioned, this isn't a political book.

It's not a culture war manifesto.

It's a call to stop.

To rest. To breathe. To return to God.

**Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. **

Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away.

Trust that God is in control.

Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship.

**In _Stop, in the Name of God,_ you'll discover: **

🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout

🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer

🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation

Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again.

That's the heartbeat of his final message.

**[To claim your copy of this life-changing book, simply make a generous gift in any amount to Turning Point USA today.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zk5hmg9v8uujq86c3bbs2bpb59f7sfioge72mss0_rp22sh2s8i6eor7c1gm2pr2c3h2bs)**

---
Charlie Kirk didn't waste his time on earth.

He left behind a family. He left behind a movement. And he left behind this truth...

For anyone ready to step off the treadmill... and walk back toward what's eternal.

Friend, thank you -- in advance -- for helping reach the next generation with truth, faith, and moral courage.

These are the very things Charlie gave his life for.

May the message he left behind lead you -- just as it led him -- to a deeper trust in God...

A stronger love for your family...

And a renewed peace in your own soul.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Reflections and resolutions
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Warren for Senate: https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/370?source=em-header&t=1001&akid=2740%2E4032634%2EwcVgYi

I hope you had a wonderful and restful holiday — and, if
it’s your thing, that you found a little time to reflect on the past year
and think about your resolutions for the next.

I’ve definitely been doing some reflecting myself. And let’s just state
the obvious: 2025 was a tough one.

The year began with Donald Trump taking power and running what has become
the most corrupt administration in American history — surpassing even his
first term.

One image kept coming back to me all year: the billionaires like Elon
Musk, Jeff Bezos, Tim Cook, and Mark Zuckerberg sitting front and center
at Trump’s inauguration, ahead of his own cabinet nominees. That image set
the tone for the year and made clear whose needs would be coming first.

That day, on Day One, was the day that Trump promised to lower costs for
families. Instead, he chose chaos and cruelty — distracting the public,
weaponizing government institutions, and ramming through policies that
hurt working people while making wealthy people even wealthier.

What did we get instead of those promised lower costs?

The Gulf of Mexico got renamed.

Elon Musk took a chainsaw to life-saving and consumer-protecting agencies
like USAID, the NIH, and the CFPB.

The White House essentially had a tacky, neon “open for business” sign put
on it, with Trump turning it into a Tesla dealership and destroying the
East Wing to make room for a ballroom to court wealthy special interests.

A reckless tariff war that drove prices up, hitting everyday essentials
hardest.

A $5 million “gold card” option, allowing the ultra-rich to buy their way
to U.S. citizenship.

At the same time, ICE agents disappeared people off the streets — masked,
unidentified, using unmarked vans, smashing car windows, and even staking
out elementary schools.

The National Guard and Marines were deployed in American cities.

They launched an unprecedented mid-decade redistricting scheme to lock in
permanent power.

Congressional Republicans fully abdicated their responsibilities, bending
the knee rather than doing their jobs.

The administration interfered with media it didn’t like — from Colbert to
Kimmel to 60 Minutes.

Republicans passed their signature policy package that rips health care
and food assistance from millions to fund tax breaks for the same
billionaires at that inauguration.

Let’s not forget the countless violations to the Constitution.

That’s only the gist of it.
I won’t sugarcoat it: this was a brutal year. Many of us stopped saying
“this has to be as bad as it gets,” because somehow it kept getting worse
day after day.

How can we, if at all, try to feel a little optimistic about 2026?

Here’s how I’m thinking about it.

Trump and his allies are doing everything they can to overwhelm us — to
rig the economy, hollow out our government, and inflict maximum pain so
people feel powerless, exhausted, and ready to give up.

There are no limits to what they think they can do to take this country
over, to humiliate people, and to try to get people to cave in and knuckle
under.

But here we are in December after a year of throwing everything they can
at us, and you know what? We’re still standing. We’re a little battered
and a little bruised. There are people who have been hurt.

But we are still standing. And more than that — we’re still fighting, and
we’re getting stronger.

We’ve learned something important: fighting back matters. Resistance
creates pressure. It forces reversals. It moves courts. It exposes
corruption. And it brings more people into the fight.

We stopped those unprecedented mid-decade gerrymandering efforts in states
like California, Missouri, and Indiana.

People took to the streets to defend neighbors targeted by ICE.

We didn’t let Kimmel or 60 Minutes be quietly silenced.

Voters across the country elected candidates who take the affordability
crisis seriously, defeating far-right MAGA opponents and demonstrating we
CAN make our economy more affordable and fairer for everyone.

Millions showed up to declare, loudly and clearly: There are no kings in
America.

Even in a year defined by chaos and cruelty, people chose to stay engaged.
That matters more than they want us to believe.

Authoritarian movements win when people decide resistance is pointless.
But all year long, we proved the opposite.

Public pressure still works.

Courts can still be moved.

Elections still matter.

Community still matters.

None of this means 2026 will be easy. But we know their plan, and we have
ours.

I understand my assignment in the Senate, and I’m committed to using every
tool I have to fight this corrupt administration. I’m resolved to help
Democrats take back the House and the Senate — and to push our party to
fight harder for working people with bold, structural economic change and
a clear, forceful rebuttal to Trump’s lies and failed policies.

As for you, I hope you’ll
join me in holding onto the belief that better things are possible — and
resolving to stay in this fight.

A clear majority of Americans disapprove of what Trump is doing. We have
the blueprint, the momentum, and the resolve to turn that disapproval into
real power.

I feel good about our chances.

As we look ahead to 2026, I want you to know what an honor it is to fight
alongside you. Thank you for staying engaged, for caring, and for showing
up. It truly matters.

[ https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3304?t=1006&akid=2740%2E4032634%2EwcVgYi ]We’re going to kick some ass in 2026. If you’re able, please consider
making a contribution before the new year to support our grassroots
movement. Your support will help fight back against this administration,
take on big, bold fights for working people — and win.

Thanks for being part of this,

Elizabeth

Fellow Conservative,

My name is Adam Schwarze, and I’m running for the U.S. Senate in Minnesota.

**I’m a former Navy SEAL who doesn’t beat around the bush.** I’ve put myself in harm's way more times than I can count because I love what this country stands for.

Leadership doesn’t start on the day one is elected; it’s a quality that one learns from a young age - you exercise it, and it develops over time. President Trump personifies it - so does Marco Rubio.

**But Tim Walz?** He lied about his service in the military, resigning in shame so he wouldn’t have to deploy to an active war zone.

That isn’t leadership, it’s cowardice.

**As governor, the Somali community in Minnesota has defrauded taxpayers of hundreds of millions of dollars, including:**

* **$300m** to pay for the therapy of children with autism, who, in fact, didn’t have autism.

* **$250m** stolen from funds meant to feed hungry children.

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

| | | | | | | Yen Bailey’s journey began with her parents, who fled war-torn Vietnam. Her father, a South Vietnamese Air Force pilot, bravely escaped the fall of Saigon by flying with his crew and dozens of Vietnamese refugees. They settled in Destin, Florida, where Yen and her brother were born and raised. Witnessing her parents' sacrifices and resilience deeply influenced Yen, inspiring her to pursue a career in law and public service.

[ ](https://yenbaileyforcongress.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=642870bb478010796c7288d8f&id=4fa5cc9867&e=58216231a8)

A Tallahassee-based attorney and Tulane University and Florida State University Law School graduate, Yen has dedicated her career to public service. She served as a Senior Attorney for the Guardian ad Litem Program and spent over 13 years as an ethics attorney at The Florida Bar. Committed to her family, Yen stepped away from her law career at the Bar to care for her elderly father.

Yen is a proud wife and mother. She cherishes time with her husband, Steve Bailey, a lawyer and professor at Florida State University and former Army Green Beret, and their two teenage sons.

Yen’s dedication to civic engagement led her to co-found Every Vote Florida, a nonprofit voter outreach organization, where she served as Vice President. She also served on the board of Friends of the LeRoy Collins Public Library System, promoting literacy and supporting public libraries in Leon County.

Yen is running for office to address the needs and challenges of the average Floridian in the panhandle, believing her opponent, Neal Dunn, has failed to do so. For years, many in the district have felt neglected and left behind by Dunn, and Yen wants to be a voice for all in Washington D.C.

With her extensive background in public service and dedication to the community, Yen Bailey offers a fresh perspective for District 2. Her journey from the daughter of immigrants to a congressional candidate embodies the American dream and the power of perseverance.

# **$26 for 2026
Let’s begin the New Year with moral clarity**
---
| | Dear friends,

As 2025 comes to a close, many of us are taking a moment to reflect — on what we’ve lived through, what we’ve learned, and what kind of future we want to help shape.

For me, this moment brings one clear conviction:

**We cannot enter the new year doing politics the same old way.

** Families across California’s 2nd District are struggling with healthcare costs, housing insecurity, and climate disasters — while Washington continues to pour billions into war instead of meeting human needs. That is not inevitable. It’s a choice.

I’m running for Congress because I believe 2026 must be a turning point — toward **moral clarity, accountability, and care for people and planet**.

As we look ahead, I’m inviting you to mark this moment with a simple, powerful act:**A $26 contribution for 2026.

** Your $26 helps us:
• Build a people-powered primary campaign
• Reach District 2 voters across rural and coastal communities
• Challenge a politics that funds war while neglecting people
• Enter 2026 with momentum, integrity, and resolve
If you’re able, I hope you’ll consider making a **$26 for 2026** contribution today.
Thank you for standing for peace and for believing in what’s possible.
With gratitude,

Rose Penelope Yee
P.S. If $26 isn’t possible right now, any amount truly helps. What matters most is starting the new year aligned with our values.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. I’m writing to you at a moment when one of our most cherished and fundamental rights — the right to vote — is under attack.
Right now, politicians in several states are trying to gerrymander their congressional maps to unfairly help their party hold onto power in the House of Representatives after the midterms. It’s a desperate, cynical move — and it’s not how democracy is supposed to work.
**In our democracy, politicians shouldn’t get to pick their voters. The people should decide who represents them. **
Since this power grab began, thousands of Americans like you have taken action to stop it. But despite this massive public outcry, extreme politicians in states like Florida and Kansas are doubling down, all in an effort to avoid accountability from voters.
**Attorney General Eric Holder and I started this organization to build a fairer democracy — _and that mission will be tested like never before in the coming months_. Now is not the time to hesitate. # Silver surges past $80 before retreating
Silver prices briefly **[topped $80 an ounce for the first time ever](https://substack.com/redirect/5aecf92c-ba9d-4441-80e6-b14c32b357a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in overnight trading before staging a dramatic reversal, sliding 7% on Monday amid volatile precious metals markets as the commodity's extraordinary 155% yearly surge showed signs of faltering.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5aecf92c-ba9d-4441-80e6-b14c32b357a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Historic milestone achieved** : Silver marked its first-ever breach above $80 per ounce, capping a remarkable rally from just over $20 at the start of 2025.
* **Reversal erases gains** : The metal plunged sharply overnight, with futures last trading around $72 amid a 7% daily drop, highlighting extreme market volatility.
* **Outperforming gold significantly** : Silver's year-to-date gain exceeded 155%, far surpassing gold's more than 70% rise despite both benefiting from safe-haven demand.
* **Driven by multiple factors** : Surge fueled by industrial demand in solar panels, EVs and electronics, plus safe-haven buying amid geopolitical risks, U.S. deficit concerns and a weaker dollar.

# Copper Rockets to Record Amid Supply Panic
In a volatile post-holiday surge, **[copper prices hit a fresh record](https://substack.com/redirect/4e599880-657e-416f-8734-1e6d6b4d12cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** near $13,000 per ton on London's exchange Monday, driven by mine outages, smelter pressures and fears of U.S. tariffs under Trump, capping its strongest year since 2009.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4e599880-657e-416f-8734-1e6d6b4d12cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Intraday Jump Hits Peak:** Prices leaped 6.6% initially--the biggest gain since 2022--before retreating to a 2% rise by midmorning.
* **New York Futures Dip:** Comex contracts fell 2% after Friday's 4.7% advance during the LME closure.
* **Chinese Plants Cut Output:** Fabrication facilities reduced or halted production amid weakening demand and price sensitivity.
* **December Rally Accelerates:** LME prices climbed over 10%, with analysts warning of overvaluation despite tariff-driven U.S. stockpiling.

# Tech Billionaires Threaten California Exodus Over Tax
Silicon Valley's **[tech titans are vowing to flee California](https://substack.com/redirect/ad4fec32-c6a5-4ce8-a4a1-631ffd5cc529?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** amid a proposed one-time 5% wealth tax on assets exceeding $1 billion, aimed at offsetting federal healthcare funding cuts if voters approve it in November.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ad4fec32-c6a5-4ce8-a4a1-631ffd5cc529?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Union backs ballot measure** : The Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West sponsors the initiative to generate billions for healthcare amid potential federal reductions.
* **Retroactive tax sparks warnings** : Applying from January 1, 2026, the levy allows payments over five years but could force billionaires to sell company shares.
* **Luckey decries forced sales** : Anduril cofounder Palmer Luckey blasts the tax for demanding billions in cash, labeling it funding for fraud and waste.
* **Ackman predicts economic ruin** : Billionaire investor Bill Ackman warns the measure could destroy Hollywood and drive entrepreneurs away, taking jobs and tax revenues elsewhere.

# Nvidia's $5B Lifeline Rescues Intel
In a surprising tech alliance, Nvidia has **[snapped up a $5 billion stake](https://substack.com/redirect/21276f58-2373-44fa-a625-759c7f79ee03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in rival Intel, injecting vital cash into the beleaguered chip giant after years of costly missteps and expansions that left its finances in tatters.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/21276f58-2373-44fa-a625-759c7f79ee03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Deal Cleared Antitrust** : U.S. regulators approved Nvidia's investment earlier this month, paving the way for the private placement transaction.
**Shares Purchased Detailed** : Nvidia acquired over 214.7 million Intel common shares at $23.28 each, totaling exactly $5 billion.
**September Announcement Recalled** : The stake was first revealed in September as a financial boost for Intel amid its production capacity struggles.
**Market Reaction Muted** : Nvidia shares dipped 1.3% in premarket trading, while Intel's remained largely unchanged following the news.

# NASA boss vows moon return in Trump era
Newly appointed NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman declared Friday that **[the United States will land astronauts on the moon again](https://substack.com/redirect/0e5b0e15-b1ca-429a-8ccc-5612ca8f4ae3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during President Donald Trump's second term, emphasizing the mission's role in unlocking vast scientific, economic and national security opportunities.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0e5b0e15-b1ca-429a-8ccc-5612ca8f4ae3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Orbital economy unlocked:** Isaacman highlighted lunar exploration as key to building an "orbital economy," including potential space data centers and infrastructure development.
**Helium-3 mining potential:** The NASA chief pointed to mining rare Helium-3 from the moon's surface, which could fuel future fusion power and drive economic growth.
**Moon base envisioned:** Plans include establishing a permanent moon base, followed by investments in nuclear power and space nuclear propulsion for deeper exploration.
**Private partners advance:** NASA collaborates with SpaceX, Blue Origin and Boeing on reusable heavy-lift vehicles and the Artemis program's upcoming crewed missions.

Nevada continues to show up and show out.

My grandfather was a five-foot-one accountant from Buffalo, New York.

He wrote me letters throughout my childhood, and one of them said this:
“David, the highest calling in life is to stand up to bullies for the people they oppress and harm.”
Like a caricature of a Jewish grandfather, he said become a lawyer AND a doctor so I could sue the pharmaceutical companies. (I didn’t go to medical school, but I have dedicated my life to fighting for regular people and holding bullies accountable.)
My grandfather moved from Buffalo to Denver to spend the last seven years of his life with our family. He is one of my greatest sources of inspiration, I miss him deeply, and I know he’d get a kick out of this campaign.
Because the things that matter most to everyday Americans – our safety, our freedoms, our livelihoods, our communities – depend on a legal system that works for all of us, not just the wealthy and well-connected.
State attorneys general are on the front lines of this fight. This is the office that can fight for the basic and fundamental rights of Coloradans. This is the office that can hold massive tech companies, health care conglomerates, and oil and gas companies accountable. This is the office that can help remedy a broken economy designed to serve only the rich.
That’s why I’m running for attorney general. And it all started with letters from my grandfather. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-25q4?refcode=x_251229_grandfather_eoy3_act]

Hi Peter!
John Willoughby here, Kelly’s husband. I hope you’re having a great holiday season!
As we approach the end of the year, we have been reflecting on the good. Despite these tumultuous and often very dark times, there have been pockets of light. I wanted to reach out to share a highlight from each month showcasing the good work Kelly has done for her constituents and beyond!
Before I dive into it, I want to give you an update on our end of year fundraising goals. Last week, our team reached out to share the news of our Republican opponent. Since then we have passed the halfway mark to our digital fundraising goals, and we are now looking to raise even more. Peter, would you consider chipping in any amount today to help us reach and exceed our end of year fundraising goals? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-email]
If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately.
Donate $10 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-email?express_lane=true&amount=10] Donate $25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-email?express_lane=true&amount=25]
Donate $50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-email?express_lane=true&amount=50] Donate $100 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-email?express_lane=true&amount=100]
Donate Other Amount [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-email]
Thank you for your consideration! Below is our 2025 Recap:
January: Kelly was sworn into the U.S. House of Representatives! It was the honor of a lifetime that our family was able to join her for this momentous day in Washington D.C. During her first month in Congress, Kelly became the first Freshman Democrat to pass a bill through the Republican controlled House.
Kelly with her family and Hakeem Jeffries at her swearing-in ceremony. [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/109390/images/people/kelly-family-swearingin-25.jpg]
February: Kelly held a telephone town hall from DC and nearly a thousand constituents dialed in. She has pushed back against Trump’s illegal actions since his first day in office, and she shared updates on her work and provided a venue for constituents to ask questions.
March: Kelly held her first in-person town hall! Over 2,000 constituents packed into Thomas Jefferson High School to hear from Kelly about her work and how they can push back against this administration.
Kelly speaking at a podium [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/109390/images/people/kelly-speaking.png]
April: Another town hall hosted by Kelly! Once again, over 1,000 constituents showed up to make their voices heard and stay engaged with their community.
May: We were lucky to have Kelly home in Minnesota for a long week over Memorial Day, and it was jam packed with campaign events and in-district meetings.
June: Kelly joined former Secretary of Veterans Affairs Denis McDonough and Minnesota’s senior Senator Amy Klobuchar for a town hall focused on veterans’ issues. It was a thoughtful conversation and an especially meaningful event for our district.
July: July was peak parade season! It was wonderful to join Kelly and see so many of you at parades across the district and feel the energy behind Kelly’s campaign.
Kelly speaking to volunteers at the Mound Spirit of The Lake Parade [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/109390/images/people/kelly-mound-parade.jpg]
August: State Fair season! Kelly’s campaign had a booth for the 12 days of the Minnesota State Fair. Kelly and volunteers passed out postcards centered around kindness and courage. Conversations at the booth were friendly and ranged from politics and current events to the Minnesota Vikings, and we are confident that fair goers left our booth feeling better about the state of the world than when they first stopped by. We are already excited for next year!
Kelly with volunteers at her state fair booth [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/109390/images/people/kelly-state-fair.jpg]
September: Another town hall hosted by Kelly—this one was focused on gun violence prevention. Kelly was joined by parents from the Annunciation Catholic School, a trauma surgeon who cared for students injured in the shooting, and brave youth advocates who are fighting for comprehensive gun reform. It was an emotional but uplifting evening.
October: Over 7 million Americans took to the streets to send a message to this administration: there are no kings in America. Kelly and I joined a march and were so inspired by everyone who came out in joyful, peaceful, and patriotic protest.
Kelly and John at the No Kings protest holding a sign that says [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/109390/images/people/kelly-morrison_no-kings.jpg]
November: Kelly celebrated Small Business Saturday by visiting incredible small businesses across the district, and highlighting her efforts on the House Small Business Committee to bring immediate relief to small businesses being adversely impacted by Trump’s chaotic tariffs.
December: This month has been busy—balancing Kelly’s work in DC and preparing for another whirlwind election year at home. Kelly is well on track to finish this year strong and hit her digital fundraising goals, but now that she has an opponent, we are hoping to surpass them.
Peter, we would be so grateful if you would be willing to chip in before the end of the year. You can do so online here. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-email]
Thank you so much for taking the time to read this email and for your continued support of Kelly. I hope you enjoy the rest of your holiday season!
With gratitude,
John Willoughby

name: Elizabeth Warren (via Working Families Party)
subject: Are you with us?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Working Families Party PAC (77 Sands St
body:
As I work in the Senate to put political and economic power in the hands of the people — where it belongs — the Working Families Party has been one of my greatest allies. | | | Hello Peter, it's Elizabeth Warren. I’ve dedicated my career to studying why families go broke and fighting to rebuild the middle class. And as I work in the Senate to put political and economic power in the hands of the people — where it belongs — the Working Families Party has been one of my greatest allies. **The Working Families Party has been on the front lines of the fight for racial and economic justice for decades — bringing working people together, electing progressive leaders, and winning real change across the country.** Together, we’re building this movement the right way — person to person, shoulder to shoulder. Not by courting billionaires or bending to giant corporations. But that’s only possible if a lot of people pitch in a little at a time to build something big. **That’s why I’m hoping you’ll make a donation today to fuel this vital work.[The end-of-year fundraising deadline is right around the corner, and the Working Families Party is still short of their $100K goal. Hitting that target will help ensure they have the resources they need to take on the big fights in 2026 and beyond.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9TYM2ujKOIJdCIDub-bHyeZ0r9V0YqSHsZ-a23c8_6RG7wmfGyUEI2Evj00Mb15lTxyNSDqnr8KjpLbkoyG442-DrhY305lwAOcG2ry_Wjj47I2SmvBLaNKtLhRn9fEfaeCm9CMmS8RxuOpaXV_hQy02hmDf9z1NlpC5bmpvEn5hW_K1dwHIJhFKHOabQ3ibiHfRxpo3ozEbU2CIWULy3LU2KRCWUXudsuD_fd7Bmx76VCT_uiJvng4wkwCPv_NNH4WJoGR8YBx4c0RgkvW-Rhp1I442q3akjOavl8pJ31sGuuJnWlMBXjHqivxL_vZQpGRI6uPCNg_qF4AiQWPXZ3RkTidKotq8e05X5q6kGwiA/4mu/XCWRcog4TMK7GR2afbxWQQ/h0/h001.FsoCopLagomThLcO5KbPEXhKPdLGRaVzZa-_Y-e3WI8)** **[Donate $10 »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9TYM2ujKOIJdCIDub-bHyeZ0r9V0YqSHsZ-a23c8_6RFRGnrhsaklllRXk3dv7qV2fxjLXFVV4ckCqzssXbWGAdoKrxiCK2YElbYkfrCP-mRed8uthwR5PLrFyTo8fAvjSsa1vJSaWTrNAlZioUF0M95NprSJVN2ReW2TcNpyZ-RIsOtTpEDa4mZH4OA3CDNj0vQN8wiU02cnJHl7qWZF7vKzgDSUXcvkirlR8I7KdrLwVbIJ4NBz4FYrmsFosSyn-pppUhtHkIR2Ghhuol-S3DqIc0hFx1fYmsB1kXXJKU0OkW9667iW_NZp836RJoXaQ5SICH0vPAFiu-WWolhtVKIBH64FkO3K58XjrNRIJC6EIGI8-dL1-ZPw7WJD5BDv/4mu/XCWRcog4TMK7GR2afbxWQQ/h1/h001.toQiZoDtBP_UXABrLJto9M_zP_6wa3YuchdMLhRb_L4)** Throughout my time in Washington, I’ve learned that when you start talking about electing candidates or enacting policies that help working people instead of wealthy people or big corporations, plenty of critics will be quick to tell you what you can’t do and what’s not possible. To tune them out and fight back, what we need is courage. Courage to stand up to billionaires and corporate donors. Courage to make the wealthiest and most powerful people in this country a little uncomfortable. Courage to shake off any instinct to show how eager we are to compromise and stand by a half-baked plan. **Year after year, I’ve been proud to watch the Working Families Party demonstrate relentless courage and an absolute unwillingness to let fear and cynicism win.** That’s how they’ve been able to help propel candidates to victory up and down the ballot, all around the country — including Zohran Mamdani, whose focus on government serving the people, not billionaires, will make life more affordable for NYC. That’s how they’ve been able to help pass policies like California’s Prop 50, which is creating a more level playing field and ensuring fairer midterm elections. That’s how they’ve been able to help recruit millions of people to show up in record-shattering numbers and say loud and clear that the American people do not bow down to kings. That’s how they’ve been able to prove the critics wrong. **The Working Families Party has big plans to keep up the fight in 2026. But those plans are only possible with the continued support of supporters like you. Let's keep working side by side to make sure the new year is a brighter one for everyone who needs a government that finally is on their side.** **[If you’re with me, I hope you’ll consider clean_body: As I work in the Senate to put political and economic power in the hands of the people — where it belongs — the Working Families Party has been one of my greatest allies. | | | Hello Peter, it's Elizabeth Warren. I’ve dedicated my career to studying why families go broke and fighting to rebuild the middle class. And as I work in the Senate to put political and economic power in the hands of the people — where it belongs — the Working Families Party has been one of my greatest allies. The Working Families Party has been on the front lines of the fight for racial and economic justice for decades — bringing working people together, electing progressive leaders, and winning real change across the country. Together, we’re building this movement the right way — person to person, shoulder to shoulder. Not by courting billionaires or bending to giant corporations. But that’s only possible if a lot of people pitch in a little at a time to build something big. That’s why I’m hoping you’ll make a donation today to fuel this vital work. Throughout my time in Washington, I’ve learned that when you start talking about electing candidates or enacting policies that help working people instead of wealthy people or big corporations, plenty of critics will be quick to tell you what you can’t do and what’s not possible. To tune them out and fight back, what we need is courage. Courage to stand up to billionaires and corporate donors. Courage to make the wealthiest and most powerful people in this country a little uncomfortable. Courage to shake off any instinct to show how eager we are to compromise and stand by a half-baked plan. Year after year, I’ve been proud to watch the Working Families Party demonstrate relentless courage and an absolute unwillingness to let fear and cynicism win. That’s how they’ve been able to help propel candidates to victory up and down the ballot, all around the country — including Zohran Mamdani, whose focus on government serving the people, not billionaires, will make life more affordable for NYC. That’s how they’ve been able to help pass policies like California’s Prop 50, which is creating a more level playing field and ensuring fairer midterm elections. That’s how they’ve been able to help recruit millions of people to show up in record-shattering numbers and say loud and clear that the American people do not bow down to kings. That’s how they’ve been able to prove the critics wrong. The Working Families Party has big plans to keep up the fight in 2026. But those plans are only possible with the continued support of supporters like you. Let's keep working side by side to make sure the new year is a brighter one for everyone who needs a government that finally is on their side. In solidarity, Elizabeth Warren Thoughts? Feedback? Peter,
2025 was the worst year yet for Lauren Boebert, and that's saying something considering the infamous Beetlejuice incident of 2023 (don't Google that in front of children).
Grab your popcorn and have a seat. Let's take a look back at:
🎬The top 5 Boebert low-lights of 2025
---
| | | 🦎 #5: The Lizard man conspiracy
Boebert pushed the ridiculous claim that Hakeem Jeffries is a "lizard man." It sounds laughable, but it comes straight out of ugly, antisemitic conspiracy culture. Reckless and unserious.
🎸#4: The Kid Rock scandal
She landed in hot water after apparently using campaign money to attend her alleged lover Kid Rock's concert. This might not even be legal.
🤬# 3: "Go back to Africa"
Ilhan Omar condemned political violence. Boebert twisted her words and told her to "go back" to Somalia. Hateful. Dangerous. Exactly on brand.
🕵🏻♀️#2: Bathroom detectives
Boebert and Nancy Mace decided to "guard" a Capitol women's restroom from trans people and ended up confronting the wrong woman entirely. Zero dignity. Zero apology.
🎃 # 1: Racist Halloween
For Halloween this year, Boebert dressed up as a "Mexican," mocking Latinos being deported by ICE. It tells you everything you need to know about her racist politics.
---
| Voters in CO-4 are exhausted. They want leadership, not conspiracies, cosplay cruelty, and bathroom inspectors.
This is why Boebert is more vulnerable than she has ever been. Boebert is only in Congress because of 546 votes. When Democrat Trisha Calvarese ran against Boebert in 2024, she delivered the best Democratic performance in district history, outperforming Kamala Harris by six points.
And Boebert's fundraising has cratered, scraping together barely $100,000 while our campaign outraised her five to one.
As we look ahead to 2026, the tide is turning and our campaign is on the brink of a shocking upset. December 31st isn't just New Year's Eve; it's our end-of-quarter deadline. We need to raise $50,000 by midnight on Wednesday to keep our fundraising advantage against Boebert.

2025 was the worst year yet for Lauren Boebert, and that's saying something considering the infamous Beetlejuice incident of 2023 (don't Google that in front of children).

🎸#4: The Kid Rock scandal
She landed in hot water after apparently using campaign money to attend her alleged lover Kid Rock's concert. This might not even be legal.

### 🤬# 3: "Go back to Africa"

Ilhan Omar condemned political violence. Boebert twisted her words and told her to "go back" to Somalia. Hateful. Dangerous. Exactly on brand.
🕵🏻♀️#2: Bathroom detectives
Boebert and Nancy Mace decided to "guard" a Capitol women's restroom from trans people and ended up confronting the wrong woman entirely. Zero dignity. Zero apology.
🎃 # 1: Racist Halloween
For Halloween this year, Boebert dressed up as a "Mexican," mocking Latinos being deported by ICE. It tells you everything you need to know about her racist politics.

Hi Derek,
John here. This has been a hard year. For a lot of folks, it feels like the ground keeps shifting under our feet. 😔
Five months ago, Trump signed Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill: Medicaid slashed to pay for tax cuts for the wealthy. Hospitals closing. Seniors pushed out of nursing homes. Millions set to lose care.
Then, Trump told Republicans to let the Obamacare subsidies expire. No reason. Premiums shot up. People are losing coverage. That wasn’t a mistake. It was a choice.
Meanwhile, the Trump administration has closed Social Security offices and cut staff. And the Treasury secretary admitted they’re working on a “backdoor” plan to privatize Social Security.
And while he holds back funding for veterans and cancer research, Trump says the affordability crisis is a “hoax.” Tell that to families paying more at the grocery store. Folks feel it every week.
Trump isn’t fighting for working families. He’s stripping the government for parts and selling them off to his rich friends.
**Long story short, that’s why we need to start preparing for the 2026 midterms now.**

## Commonsense Corner:
---
There’s no way around it: 2026 is a make-or-break moment for Republicans. As Tim has routinely pointed out, we’ve got one of the weakest majorities in history, and we’re not using it the way we should be. If we don’t start delivering on the America First agenda faster, we risk handing the keys to the castle right back to the Democrats. clean_body: Burchett Bulletin will keep you updated on the important issues and goings-on in our campaign, in Tennessee, and in our country.| | | | | | Commonsense Corner: There’s no way around it: 2026 is a make-or-break moment for Republicans. As Tim has routinely pointed out, we’ve got one of the weakest majorities in history, and we’re not using it the way we should be. The party of supporters gathered to watch the votes roll in together. My
hardworking staff tracking every precinct. Holding my wife Lisa’s hand as
the results showed a much closer outcome than anticipated.

Before Election Night, everyone assumed our campaign had it in the bag.
The polls were on our side. Some news outlets had even called this
campaign “unbeatable.”

And then we came less than 20,000 votes away from losing. It took three
days to learn the final results. I won by just 0.8% of the vote.

I tell you this story because I know we can’t take anything for granted.
And with so much on the line next year, we can’t sit back and hope for the
best.

So I’ve got to ask you,

A bureaucrat who assumed no one was watching. An institution that believed it was above accountability. **They were wrong. And we have the footage to prove it.** Here are five investigations from 2025 that changed the game:
* **1\. THE $100 BILLION FEDERAL CONTRACTING SCAM (October)**
* We exposed ATI Government Solutions exploiting the SBA's 8(a) minority contracting program — outsourcing 80% of their work while pocketing over $100 million in no-bid contracts. This wasn't a one-off. It was a systemic scheme across multiple agencies.
* **THE RESULT:** SBA suspension. $253 million in contracts halted. A $9 billion Treasury Department audit. Seven additional companies suspended. And a 15-year review of 8(a) contracts across every federal agency.
* **2\. GAO DATA THEFT CONFESSION (November)**
* A GAO director admitted on hidden camera that staff "stole and backed up" vaccine data specifically to block RFK Jr.'s HHS reforms. They weren't just resisting policy — they were breaking federal law.
* **THE RESULT:** The director's profile was scrubbed. A federal investigation was launched. And the nation finally saw what "deep state resistance" actually looks like.
* **3\. NIH PORTRAIT DESTRUCTION (December)**
* NIH contractor Joseph Olmert confessed on camera to destroying official portraits of President Trump, Vice President Vance, RFK Jr., and Dr. Jay Bhattacharya. That's a potential 10-year federal felony — destruction of government property.
* **THE RESULT:** Contractor FIRED. NIH internal investigation launched. And a national conversation about the defiance embedded in our federal agencies.
* **4\. GEORGETOWN PROFESSOR EXPOSED (December)**
* We caught a Georgetown professor on hidden camera calling Black conservatives "coons" and mocking "stupid white people." When we confronted him, he tried to assault our cameraman. Police were called.
* **THE RESULT:** Georgetown wiped his bio from their website. The footage went viral — over 2 million views. And elite academic bias was laid bare for all to see.
* **5\. INSIDE EPSTEIN'S ISLAND (May-December)**
* We released the first-ever footage from inside Jeffrey Epstein's private island mansion. We confronted a DOJ Deputy Chief who admitted plans to redact Republicans from the Epstein files. We published unredacted photos that Democrats tried to hide.
* **THE RESULT:** DOJ was forced to respond. Media outlets issued corrections. Joe Rogan covered our findings. And the truth about elite corruption reached millions who had been kept in the dark.

That means we only need to flip three U.S. House seats next year to take back the chamber. And we’re already laying the groundwork to make that happen. ** | If we take back the House next year, that majority will go a long way toward restraining the extremist agenda of the incoming Trump administration (just like it did in 2018!). Here’s our game plan to win back the majority in 2026 with Democratic pro-choice women: Recruitment: We’ve got EMILYs List regional staff deployed all across the country to scout Democratic pro-choice women who want to make a difference in their communities and shape the national conversation around Democratic values in 2026. Building campaigns: We’re already kicking off resume drops and organizing workshops for new and returning campaign staff, as part of our tried-and-true recruitment and training process to ensure our candidates have the strongest teams behind them. Investing in incumbents: We know that early money is absolutely crucial to our candidates, because that’s how they build the foundation to raise even more money down the line (in fact, it’s in our name: E arlyM oneyI sLi ke Y east!). That’s why we’re identifying which of our incumbents will need the most support to hold their seats next cycle and making a plan to get them the resources they need. | | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. | | | [](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkUGOnTAMhk8TdjwRhySTBYuqT0hdzGy7RMYxEA0kNAmv169o5wLdWfbnT7L_n-_TO4Y9xPUDDx7oFaZcprrxnNInbZj3wDsvdeYtRD9BB7qV0IK7Mdn4gbxR0PAgrbFdD52CZhuUXpRxSFJZv4DXJNHRPJMB14NlbMJwmySAA9l1YB9uRqVBo1u00-zfRN9dp8fK5UEpFs4vrOHFIcZ0Vyk-KB3NPmy1nkWobwJGAWNhujI_MLJP9SYEjPXKMcS1PVOItb0KChjBae3YUYuq922PpFuUxrTSGTJvFlnyItRY0pWJJ0qehXp-__FhnbJagLnqMR3sw3UI9eQDw_7V_Lch1HPD7LF8Tki_vkaEx4lhjUI9S6gxrdP94iYP_vwd9j0UY0Xfrbfs7231v8N4DfAnAAD__wITmAk)
